methodology.execution: Serial cases; alternating before/after order per paired trial; process-wide CPU includes operation loop overhead
methodology.compilation: Extracted source transpiled with recorded TypeScript compiler to ES2022/CommonJS and classic React JSX; no Next.js production build or React Compiler transform
methodology.summaries: Median batch wall/CPU divided by batch iterations; raw paired samples retained
methodology.metrics: Case-supplied measured numeric outputs from actual-source fixture operations
methodology.memory: Heap/RSS process snapshots per batch, not allocation counts or peak/production memory; deltas can be negative and shared process state affects RSS
methodology.io: No production latency claim. Case fixture descriptions must identify simulated I/O, clocks, dependency stubs and data scales

results.title: Bookmark membership preserves database ordering with per-query sets
results.fixture: Small: 3 widgets x 8 references; large: 30 widgets x 240 references across 2,000 possible app IDs. Shared DB result is mocked in reverse order; distinct query keys are deduplicated. One symmetric setImmediate turn after each operation releases completed async request resources; its wall/CPU overhead is included.

results.title: Docker repository import keeps normalized first-seen images
results.fixture: Small: 24 unique images + 24 duplicate tags, 12 configured repositories; large: 1,000 + 1,000 duplicate tags, 500 configured repositories. IDs are deterministic; real provider and version normalization functions execute.

results.title: App prefetch shares a first-match index and retains missing-app errors
results.fixture: Small: 24 apps; large: 2,000 apps. Reverse-order DB rows, one duplicate widget. Promise/database and query-key scheduling are mocked; no network latency is included. One symmetric setImmediate turn after each operation releases completed async request resources; its wall/CPU overhead is included. Batches contain 5 operations to bound simultaneous promise allocation pressure.

results.title: Immutable sort avoids an explicit array copy
results.fixture: Small: 24 rows sorted by name ascending; large: 2,000 rows sorted by CPU descending, with duplicate sort keys. Timed inputs are mutable dense arrays like production filter/map results. Separate frozen fixtures verify immutability; iterator instrumentation counts explicit spread copies separately from timing.
